name: Meesho Ltd
title: Meesho Ltd - 544632 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Meesho is an asset-light marketplace with no capacity to add; the read is margin repair from logistics normalisation (CM exit rate 4%) and ad monetisation, but LTM FCF and CFO remain negative with no guidance given.

summary.headline: Meesho says logistics disruption in Q2–Q3 FY26 is behind it; Q4 contribution margin exit rate of 4% is the new baseline.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a strong quarter, with contribution margin up about 170 bps QoQ, of which roughly 110 bps came from lower logistics cost. The 145 bps one-time logistics headwind was concentrated in Q2 and Q3 FY26 and attributed to short-term capacity building during 3PL consolidation around May 2025. Ad revenue as a percentage of NMV rose QoQ, while reported revenue per order looked flat partly due to accounting changes (first-order discounts now netted against revenue) and a higher prepaid mix. Management gave no EBITDA break-even or FCF timing guidance; it pointed to LTM FCF as the guiding metric, and Q4 cash balance fell about INR300 crore, which management partly attributed to tax payments expected to be recovered.

financial_highlights.metric: Logistics cost benefit in contribution margin

financial_highlights.change: Stated as behind the company; not expected to recur
Stable in a 58%–60% range for last three years
Partly due to tax payments reclassified out of cash

financial_highlights.value: About INR47 in FY26 vs about INR57 in FY24
financial_highlights.change: Decline attributed to logistics cost and accounting changes

segments.name: Valmo (in-house logistics)
segments.commentary: Management says there is no target share; about 50–55% of orders are currently fulfilled via Valmo per analyst estimate, and volume goes to the most cost-efficient partner per lane. Management plans sort-centre automation over the next few years, possibly via partners rather than own capex.

segments.name: Ads (marketplace)
segments.commentary: More than two-thirds of sellers by GMV are active on ads; ad catalogue count up over 40% YoY. Advertiser budgets over the last year grew more than double, and pricing increases are deferred until steady-state ad revenue is higher.

segments.name: Meesho Mall
segments.commentary: Focused on value brands for mass India; contribution margin is deliberately below the core marketplace during an investment phase to onboard brands.

guidance_outlook: No specific short-term EBITDA guidance given; management pointed to LTM FCF as the guiding metric.
Management expects quarterly FCF to keep improving with margin and growth, with the FY26 logistics impact carried into the next few quarters.

Contribution margin baseline is the 4% Q4 exit rate; further improvement expected to come from ad revenue and partial restoration of fulfilment margin, slower than Q3 to Q4 gains over the next two quarters.
Tech and people costs expected to grow slower than NMV, with operating leverage over the short and long term; cloud costs move in 2–3 year contract cycles.
Plans to invest significantly more in rural user acquisition over the next year, subject to return-on-investment thresholds.
Management did not commit to a share target for Valmo or a specific ad spend (AMP) percentage of NMV.
capex_capacity: Valmo sort-centre automation is a stated focus area over the next few years; funding model (own capex vs partner-built facilities) not yet pinned down.
Short-term capacity added at higher rates during 3PL consolidation (around May 2025) has largely been unwound, per management.
Multiple Valmo cost innovations are being rolled out; quantification deferred to coming quarters.
Cloud contract renegotiation every 2–3 years to capture scale discounts.
demand_pricing: First-year user frequency has roughly doubled over three years; mature cohorts (FY24 and before) reach about 15 orders over roughly three years, per management.
Prepaid share rising, lowering COD costs; BNPL is early-stage and not yet a material driver of the shift.
CAC declined, which management attributes to AI-led tools (voice agent Vaani) and pricing improvements that lowered the barrier to first order in rural areas.
Ads ROAS described as among the best in the industry; pricing not yet increased, with management stating it will raise ad pricing at the right time.
Seller concentration continues to fall; 960,000 sellers referenced by an analyst, with growing non-GST seller onboarding.

qa_highlights.question: Will management target a lower share of in-sourced (Valmo) logistics to expand contribution margin further?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhiresh Bansal said there is no specific target; the current cost structure, around 50%, is the most optimised, and mix is adjusted as costs change.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow turn more negative even as margins improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited one-offs from past periods and quarter-end NMV timing; it pointed to LTM FCF and offered to share a reconciliation.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue per order fallen while ad revenue is rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is now netted for first-order discounts and prepaid mix is rising; prepaid orders are net neutral to contribution margin, so management prefers contribution margin as the trend metric.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cash balance decline of about INR300 crore be explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Quarter-end NMV timing causes volatility, and some taxes paid are expected to be refunded, so the net cash figure was adjusted for them.

qa_highlights.question: Would BNPL drive lower COD share?
qa_highlights.answer: BNPL is early; the COD reduction so far has come from prepaid pricing and discounts.

qa_highlights.question: When will ad pricing rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will raise pricing at the right time; first it wants more sellers activated and budgets scaled (budgets more than doubled in a year).

risks_watch: Quarterly cash flow volatility and negative CFO trend in Q2–Q4 FY26; reconciliation promised.
Ad pricing increases are deferred, so ad revenue growth depends on seller adoption and budgets.
Logistics cost recovery depends on 3PL consolidation and partner pricing; the 145 bps one-off is management's view and needs verification next quarter.
Rising user acquisition spend in rural areas could weigh on below-contribution margins if CAC rises.
Non-GST seller onboarding is growing fast; management says returns remain stable, but this is not yet proven in disclosed data.
Possible inflation impact on consumer AOV and frequency; management views value-focused players as potential gainers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on unit economics, ad ROAS and user growth, but evasive on specific targets: no EBITDA break-even date, no Valmo share goal, no ad spend percentage, and no FCF timing commitment. Management was most cautious on cash flow, attributing the weak quarterly figures to timing and one-offs.
key_quotes: So actually, we do not again take a specific goal on what should be the advertising spend.
So NMV is on the basis of orders delivered and not returned.
I think LTM FCF, which you rightly kind of pointed out, has been the guiding sort of line item.

growth.why: No numeric revenue or EBITDA guidance was given; management only pointed to a 4% contribution margin exit rate as baseline and to LTM FCF as the guiding metric, with improvement from ads and fulfilment margin described qualitatively and no capacity or order commitments quantified.
